claims.text: Adding 15% Cr, 15% Mo, and 10% W to an otherwise equiatomic HEA increases its refractory-element content.
The specified Cr-Mo-W modification will enhance elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance relative to standard equiatomic HEAs.
The specified Cr-Mo-W modification will enhance elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance relative to conventional structural alloys.
An equiatomic HEA without elevated refractory-metal content exhibits baseline tribo-corrosion degradation under high-temperature conditions.
Increasing refractory-element content promotes formation of a robust high-temperature oxide scale.
The oxide film formed by the modified HEA is stable and protective at high temperatures.
The protective oxide film acts as a barrier against mechanical wear.
The protective oxide film acts as a barrier against corrosive attack.
The modified HEA will degrade significantly more slowly under tribo-corrosive conditions than standard equiatomic HEAs and conventional structural alloys.
The modified HEA will form a superior and more adherent oxide scale than standard equiatomic HEAs and conventional structural alloys.
Standard equiatomic HEAs show rapid degradation under combined high-temperature and tribo-corrosion conditions.
Conventional structural alloys show rapid degradation under combined high-temperature and tribo-corrosion conditions.
The expected performance benefit is contingent on attaining the specified refractory-element content.
Lower refractory-element additions may fail to produce an oxide scale adequate for improved tribo-corrosion resistance.
